newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka approves new shipping policy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka approves new shipping policy.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government has approved a policy to expand the island's role as a shipping hub for south Asia, Ports and Shipping Minister Mohamed Ashraff said on Monday.
"Till now we only looked at Colombo as the region's hub," he said in a speech at the opening of an oil berth at Colombo port.

"Now the entire island is going to be a hub for south Asia with the simultaneous development of the existing (southern) Galle port, a brand new container port at Galle and a new jetty in (eastern) Trincomalee," he said, without giving details of the policy.

Ashraff said the government was holding talks with a consortium led by units of Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) to lease the port's Queen Elizabeth Quay and develop it into a container terminal.
Colombo port's revenue increased to nine billion rupees ($152 million) in 1996 from 4.9 billion rupees in 1993, Ashraff also said.
Profit before tax went up to 2.5 billion rupees in 1996 from 949 million rupees in 1993, he added.
The new oil berth, built at a cost of 2.2 billion rupees, most of which was met by a Japanese soft loan, can handle ships of up to 60,000 tonnes.
The facility has nine pipelines, laid by NKK Corporation of Japan, for loading and discharging products like crude oil, fuel oil, gas oil, naphtha, bunker fuel and liquid petroleum gas.
The oil berth was built by Penta-Ocean/Wakachiku Joint Venture, contractors for the port's Jaye Container Terminal.
